notes: pair: narrative + supertype Message, each trimmed and folded like the room profile's pairs; is_message is what isMessage must answer.

characters and members: the world every case reads. characters is the world's Characters (id to name), the names a reader shows; members is the members list as GET members returns its rows (the owner's row has id null, matching a created_by of null).

addressed: isAddressedTo(message, character); an empty character id ("") is never addressed, not even by an empty characters. An empty characters addresses every member only when the message's x_served_trimmed (served by keel, a list of field names) does not name characters; with it, the message is addressed to no Character the reader is given. unseen: isAddressedTo as above beside hasUnseenRecipients(message) as unseen_recipients, true when x_served_trimmed names characters (someone the reader cannot see is a recipient; never who or how many). everyone: isToEveryone(message, keyless) as to_everyone and hasUnseenRecipients(message, keyless) as unseen_recipients, keyless true for a body served without a credential (the keyless public reader, which keel never serves the mark): isToEveryone is true only for a message with an empty characters, no mark naming characters, and a credential; hasUnseenRecipients is null (unknown) for a keyless body. A case without keyless (unseen) has a credential. A keyless body's null narrator keeps senderStatus unverifiable, never unseen: with no mark, the reader cannot tell nobody from someone hidden (keyless-null-narrator-is-unverifiable). A Note (note_pair) is not a message and is addressed to nobody. sent_by: isSentBy(message, character), whether narrator is the character; a message with no narrator is sent by nobody.

recipients: recipientsOf(message) as recipients: the ids of characters, each Character once, in the order of its first place (a list served with one Character twice is read once, in its first place); a Note, or any Narrative that is not a message, has none.

sender: senderStatus(message, members) is status; a case with members null is a world whose members list the reader cannot read. status unseen is a null narrator beside an x_served_trimmed naming narrator (a sender the reader cannot see, shown as from someone you cannot see), distinct from unverifiable for a null narrator without the mark; claimed is the narrator (null: none, shown as from nobody, or unseen); written_by, on a mismatch, is the author's Character.

mark: readMarkOf(relations, character, members): of the Read relations given, the id of the reader's mark: actor the reader, written by the reader's own hand (the sender rule on actor: verified) or carrying no created_by at all (a folder, an export: no hand to check), and, where it carries changed_by, last changed by its creator (changed_by equal to created_by; a changed_by with no created_by beside it is ignored); the newest updated_at when there are several, whatever their order in the list; null when the reader has none, and always null for an empty character id. keyless true is a body served without a credential (the keyless public reader, served no created_by or changed_by): no mark counts there, so readMarkOf(relations, character, members, keyless) is null; a case without keyless has a credential, or is a folder.

order: created_at, read as an instant (an offset and a fraction of a second count; a time with no offset is UTC) in the one form the page gives, matched whole, every part in its range, a year any four of the digits 0 to 9 from 0000 on the Gregorian calendar run on in both directions (the leap rule on the year's number as written, so 0000 is a leap year), and a fraction counted to its sixth digit, and two at the same instant keep the order of the list given (the server's list order); a created_at that cannot be read as a date and time (absent, null, 09:61, a word) comes after every readable one, in the order of the list given.

unread: unreadFor(messages, reader, read_mark, members) for reader: messages only (a Note never), addressed to the reader, not sent by the reader, not on the mark; as ids in created_at order; read_mark null is a reader with no mark. Sent by the reader: a message with no created_by key (a folder, an export) is the reader's own when its narrator is the reader; one with created_by is the reader's own only when senderStatus against members is verified (a mismatch, an author off the list, no members list: unread for the Character it claims). A case without members reads the world's members; members null is a reader with no members list.

thread: every message whose chain of parent_narrative reaches root, the root included, as ids in created_at order; a parent_narrative that is not a string (a number, null, an object) ends the chain there.

edited: editedBy(message, members) as {edited, by}: edited is true when the message carries changed_by and it is not equal to its created_by (an absent created_by is never equal; null is the owner on both); by is the Character of the changed_by membership on members, null when it plays none, is off the list, or there is no list, and null whenever edited is false. The sender's answer never changes for an edit.

note: noteOf(notes, character, members) is line: of the narratives given, the id of the Character's line: a Note (note_pair, trimmed and folded like pair) whose narrator is the character, neither hidden (hidden true) nor proposed (x_review_proposed an object), and in its author's hand (no created_by key: trusted, a folder; with created_by: senderStatus verified); the newest by the order above whose created_at can be read, or the last in the list when none can; null when there is none. A case without members reads the world's members.
Every case has a kind and a name; a reader dispatches on kind. A case's note is prose for the reader of the fixture, never an input.

cases.name: recipients-a-repeated-recipient-is-answered-once-in-its-first-place
cases.note: characters names the second Character, then the first, then the second again: a message names each Character once, so the second is one recipient, answered in her first place, before the first. A reader that kept the last place would answer the first Character first; one that read the repeat twice would answer three recipients.

cases.name: recipients-a-narrative-that-is-not-a-message-has-none
cases.note: A Narrative with supertype Story is not a message, so it has no recipients: its characters are the people it is about. A reader answers recipients only for what the pair names a message.

message.name: Message 6
message.story: Ada, tell Mara (019a3b10-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a2) the harbour is closed.

cases.name: mark-changed-by-without-created-by-is-ignored
cases.note: The line between this and mark-in-a-folder-without-created-by-counts: a mark that carries neither created_by nor changed_by is a folder's and counts; one that carries changed_by names a writer, and a writer with no creator beside it is no hand to check, so it is ignored (as mark-changed-by-another-hand-is-ignored, where the creator is there and differs).

cases.name: keyless-empty-recipients-is-never-asserted-to-everyone
cases.note: Served without a credential: keel leaves out the ids this reader may not see and serves no mark, so an empty list is to everyone or to someone the reader cannot see, and the reader cannot tell which.

cases.name: keyless-null-narrator-is-unverifiable
cases.note: A keyless body is served no mark, so its reader cannot tell a message sent by nobody from one whose sender is hidden: the status stays unverifiable, never unseen.

cases.name: taken-character-verifies-the-new-members-message
cases.note: Two memberships over one Character in sequence: the removed member's row keeps Fen, and a new person took Fen after the removal.

cases.name: trimmed-narrator-is-unseen
cases.note: Distinct from unverifiable-no-narrator: a null narrator beside a mark naming narrator is a sender this reader cannot see, not a message sent by nobody.

cases.name: note-is-addressed-to-nobody-even-when-its-characters-names-the-reader
cases.note: A Note has no recipients whatever its characters holds: isAddressedTo is false for an id its characters names, the same as recipientsOf being empty.

cases.name: note-is-never-in-a-thread
cases.note: threadOf leaves a Note out even when its parent_narrative names the root: only a message belongs to the chain.

cases.name: note-is-never-unread-even-when-its-characters-names-the-reader
cases.note: A Note is never unread, even when its characters names the reader; the message beside it is.

cases.name: note-hidden-is-any-mark-not-only-true
cases.note: The hidden mark reads as hidden for any value but absent, null or false: a Note with hidden 'yes' is left out the same as hidden true; the newest that is not hidden stands.

cases.name: note-newest-listed-last-is-the-authors-line
cases.note: The newest Note is the last in the list: a reader that keeps the first-listed (the oldest) Note answers the other one.

cases.name: created-at-with-an-offset-and-a-fraction-is-read-as-an-instant
cases.note: created_at is read as an instant: 10:59:59.999+02:00 is 08:59:59.999Z, before 09:00:00Z, which is before 09:00:00.500Z. Compared as text the order is the other way round (09:00:00.500Z, 09:00:00Z, then 10:59:59.999+02:00), and the list order is a third.

cases.name: mark-on-a-keyless-body-is-ignored
cases.note: The same mark as mark-in-a-folder-without-created-by-counts, served without a credential: the keyless public reader is served no created_by or changed_by on any body, so a mark there carries neither because the hands were taken off, not because it is a folder's, and it is ignored.

cases.name: created-at-with-no-offset-is-read-as-utc
cases.note: A created_at with no offset is read as UTC wherever the reader runs: 10:00:00+02:00 is 08:00Z, 09:00:00 is 09:00Z and 10:30:00+01:00 is 09:30Z. Compared as text the order is 09:00:00, then 10:00:00+02:00, then 10:30:00+01:00; a reader that reads the time with no offset as its own local time gives that order east of Greenwich and another west of it. The case cannot catch a reader whose own clock is UTC.

cases.name: created-at-in-any-other-form-cannot-be-read
cases.note: Only the page's one form is read, matched whole. R1 (a lower-case t and z) and R2 (ten digits of a fraction) are in it: R2 is 08:00:00.123456Z and R1 09:00Z. X1 a date alone, X2 a space where the T is, X3 a time without its seconds, X4 an offset without its colon and X5 a time followed by a line break and X6 a year in Arabic-Indic digits (the page's digits are 0 to 9) are not, and come after, in the order given. A language's own date parser reads X1 to X4; a pattern tested with a dollar sign and a plain match reads X5 and puts it first.

cases.name: created-at-with-a-part-out-of-its-range-cannot-be-read
cases.note: Each of Y1 (30 February), Y2 (hour 24) and Y3 (second 60) is in the page's form with a part out of its range: none can be read, and they come after R, in the order given.

cases.name: created-at-fraction-counts-to-its-sixth-digit
cases.note: A fraction counts to its sixth digit and later digits are dropped: P (.0000019) and Q (.0000011) are both 10:00:00.000001Z, one instant, and keep the order given; S (.000002) comes after. A reader that compares seven digits gives Q, P, S; one that rounds to the sixth gives Q, then S and P as one instant in the order given.

cases.name: created-at-at-either-end-of-the-years-is-read
cases.note: A year is any four of the digits 0 to 9, 0000 among them, on the Gregorian calendar run on in both directions, and every text in the form and in range is an instant: E3 (0000-01-01T00:00:00+01:00) is 23:00Z on the day before E2 (0000-01-01T00:00:00Z), and E1 (9999-12-31T23:00:00-02:00) is 01:00Z on the first day of year 10000. E4 (0000-02-29T00:00:00Z) is a day that month has: the leap rule is taken on the year's number as written, and 0000 is divisible by 400. So E3, E2, E4, R, E1. A reader whose date type cannot hold year 0 or a time past 9999 puts E1, E2 or E3 among the unreadable.
